rationale: Every tight-target run met timing with positive slack (T_eff = target minus 0.12-0.56 ns), so T_eff tracks the target; loose targets turn I/O-port-limited (T_eff 9.5-10.1). Push the target to the range floor (0.45 -> 8.49 ns, just under the best T_eff 8.57). The two best runs (des, md5) both used cap213 (largest signoff margin ~+0.55 ns, 0 hold buffers) and post-GRT timing repair; tight stock/orfs runs kept only +0.12-0.30 ns, two needing 82-242 hold buffers. Keep DELAY 4 (best run) for faster logic at the tighter target, and skip routability-driven spreading since congestion is low (DRC converges to 0). Hold, DRC and slew/cap (bar 953) are not binding; other knobs left to TPE.
